summary: Negrofoot tower site in Hanover County, Virginia; the association marks the site gone and lists the tower as relocated to Field Day of the Past in Goochland County. No source describes the site now.

events.note: Association lists the tower as relocated from Negrofoot (Hanover County) to Field Day of the Past (Goochland County); no date given

evidence.supports: Negrofoot tower in Hanover County; site marked Tower Gone
tower relocated to Field Day of the Past, Goochland County
evidence.quote: Field Day of the Past (Relocated Negrofoot) Goochland 37.67619 -77.67142 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: place is an unincorporated community in Hanover County, Virginia
evidence.quote: Negro Foot is an unincorporated community in Hanover County, Virginia, United States.

evidence.supports: a tavern was located on the Negrofoot property
evidence.quote: A tavern was also located on the property Negrofoot (DHR 42-54).

evidence.supports: Negrofoot described as a major stagecoach stop at a busy crossroads connecting to Route 33
evidence.quote: Sited at a busy crossroads connecting to Route 33, Negrofoot was a major stagecoach stop.

evidence.supports: Field Day of the Past began in 1992 in Goochland County
evidence.quote: In the summer of 1992, a few steam and gas engine enthusiasts gathered for an informal discussion on the possibility of hosting a steam and gas engine show in Goochland County, Virginia.
hosted their first show in October of that year

evidence.quote: This year, Field Day of the Past relocated its operations to Mount Airy Farm in Church Road, Va (Dinwiddie County)

sources.title: Survey of Historic Resources, Hanover County, Virginia

notes_for_editor: The Negrofoot tower's own build date, design and height are not in any readable source, so the story covers only the place, the relocation and the current listing. The 1990 DHR survey describes a Negrofoot tavern and stagecoach stop; it does not say the tavern stood at the lookout's site, and the story does not claim it did. The association's table marks this site Tower Gone, which matches the record's relocated status only loosely. A Waymarking page (https://www.waymarking.com/waymarks/WM6Q0E) places the original tower on Route 54 in Hanover County, with coordinates that match this record; it is NOT cited because our reader cannot extract its text for quote checks. A Facebook group post mentions a fire tower site NW of Richmond near Negrofoot; it was unreadable and is not cited.
